The test image shows a very young soybean seedling at early emergence. Key observations:
- Very early seedling stage (just emerged from soil)
- Wet/moist soil conditions
- One seedling appears to have collapsed/rotted cotyledons
- The seed/cotyledon on the right appears brown and decayed with soft rot appearance
- Pre/post-emergence damping off pattern

This strongly suggests Pythium damping off or Rhizoctonia. Let me check reference images for these and related diseases.

The Pythium damping off reference images are a very strong match — nearly identical scene with very young seedlings in wet soil with rotted/collapsed seedlings. Let me check a few more for thoroughness.

The comparison is clear. The test image shows:
- Extremely young seedlings at the soil surface in wet conditions
- One seedling with green/healthy cotyledons emerging
- An adjacent seed/seedling that has rotted and collapsed (soft, brown decay)
- Wet, mucky soil — classic high-moisture damping off environment

**Pythium damping off** is the definitive match:
- The Pythium reference collage shows nearly identical scenes: very early post-emergence seedlings in wet soil with rotted/failed cotyledons
- Rhizoctonia shows more developed plants with reddish-brown dry cankers — doesn't fit
- Fusarium, Charcoal Rot, SDS, Brown Stem Rot all show mature plant/root symptoms — clearly not applicable here
